title: Polymorphism Through Base References
learningObjectives: Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: Polymorphism allows code to use a base interface while the actual derived object supplies overridden behavior. References and pointers enable dynamic dispatch; object-by-value can slice derived state.
understand.whyItMatters: Polymorphism lets clients depend on abstractions rather than concrete types.
understand.explain: Use base references/pointers, avoid slicing, and ensure objects outlive the references.

examples.title: Base reference dispatch
examples.code: struct Animal{virtual void sound()const{std::cout<<\"?\";}virtual ~Animal()=default;};\nstruct Cat:Animal{void sound()const override{std::cout<<\"Meow\";}};\nCat c;Animal& a=c;a.sound();
examples.explanation: Reference dispatch uses the actual object type.

examples.title: Avoid slicing
examples.code: struct Base{virtual int id()const{return 1;}};\nstruct Derived:Base{int id()const override{return 2;}};\nDerived d;Base& ref=d;std::cout<<ref.id();
examples.explanation: A base reference preserves derived dynamic behavior; copying into a base value would slice.

examples.title: Pointer polymorphism
examples.code: struct Shape{virtual int sides()const=0;virtual ~Shape()=default;};\nstruct Triangle:Shape{int sides()const override{return 3;}};
examples.explanation: A base pointer/reference can call a derived implementation.

examples.title: Interface collection
examples.explanation: Smart-pointer collection can own different derived objects through a base interface; include memory/vector.

examples.title: Virtual behavior test
examples.code: struct Base{virtual const char* name()const{return \"Base\";}virtual ~Base()=default;};\nstruct Child:Base{const char* name()const override{return \"Child\";}};\nChild c;Base* p=&c;std::cout<<p->name();
examples.explanation: The base pointer calls the overridden method.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five Polymorphism Through Base References examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating polymorphism through base references in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

questions.prompt: Base object copied from derived causes?
questions.explanation: Copying base value discards derived portion.

questions.prompt: Base pointer calls overridden function if?
